payload.text: A cart starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 1.50 m/s² for 4.00 s.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Design a feasible measurement that tests the governing relation; identify the independent variable, dependent variable, and one control.

criteria.description: Correctly identifies elapsed time as the independent variable, the cart's resulting velocity (or displacement) as the dependent variable, and holds the cart's mass and track incline/friction constant as the control.
required_evidence: elapsed time as the independent variable
final velocity (or displacement) as the dependent variable
cart mass and track incline held constant as the control
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why treating the acceleration as constant throughout the 4.00 s interval, and assuming friction is negligible, justifies using the kinematics equations to obtain v and Δx.

criteria.description: Correctly cites the constant-acceleration kinematics equations as the governing principle and states that friction/air resistance is negligible so acceleration stays constant.
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.
